messages.content: Write a short scene in modern American English between two longtime adult friends having a casual conversation. Make the scene feel specific and lived-in. Let the characters' dialogue and small actions reveal their relationship. Avoid generic filler phrases, clichés, broad summaries of their friendship, and narration that tells the reader they are close instead of showing it.

“You're doing that thing again.”

Alex didn't look up from her phone. “What thing?”

“The thing where you read the same sentence six times and pretend you're understanding it.”

“I understand it.”

“You've been staring at that screen for two minutes.”

“It's a complicated sentence.”

Jordan leaned over to look. “That's the menu.”

Alex blinked.

Jordan waited.

“Oh.”

“Yeah.”

“I was wondering why the chapter on economics mentioned mozzarella sticks.”

Jordan laughed. “You need sleep.”

“I need food.”

“You had dinner.”

“That was hours ago.”

“It was forty minutes ago.”

“Exactly. Hours.”

Jordan shook her head and took the phone out of Alex's hand before she could start scrolling again.

“Hey.”

“Go to bed.”

“Give me my phone.”

“Nope.”

“You're abusing your power.”

“I have no power.”

“You've got my phone.”

“Temporary power.”

Alex narrowed her eyes. “You realize I'm getting this back eventually.”

“Probably.”

“And when I do, I'm changing your contact name.”

“To what?”

“Something humiliating.”

Jordan smiled. “You've been threatening that for three years.”

“I'm waiting for the right name.””
